title: Precision-granular kernel catalog and prefill orchestration to minimize dequant overhead
creator: Priya Nair
description:
Goal: Build a precision-granular kernel catalog and a prefill orchestration layer that reduces dequantization overhead for INT8/FP8 model paths while preserving generation quality and latency SLOs.

Scope:
- Catalog schema for kernels: per-operator (attn, matmul, epilogue), precision supported (INT8/FP8/FP16), fused options (dequant+epilogue fused), memory footprint, preferred sequence length ranges, batch size tradeoffs, streaming suitability.
- Runtime scoring function that returns a ranked list of kernel variants for a request based on (model metadata, sequence length, KV cache hit rate, target latency SLO, cost tier).
- Prefill orchestration that co-schedules prefill work to warm KV cache and choose kernel handoff points that avoid unnecessary dequant/requant cycles.
- Telemetry hooks to record token-level cost, dequant calls, kernel switches, and quality deltas per prompt set.

Non-goals: building new quantization schemes or retraining models. This ticket focuses on runtime selection and scheduling.

Design decisions and constraints:
- Prefer fused dequant+epilogue kernels when available for streaming prefill to avoid N extra memory copies; fall back to staged kernels if fusion causes >3% quality regression on eval set.
- Use an empirical latency-cost tradeoff model: offline microbenchmarks provide kernel throughput/latency matrices per device and sequence length; runtime sampling updates scores.
- Provide a conservative safety margin for tail-latency SLOs: if predicted P99 exceeds SLO, prefer higher-precision kernel or smaller microbatching.

Acceptance criteria:
- End-to-end P90 generation latency reduced by at least 8% on INT8 paths for batch sizes 1-8 on our standard benchmark (lm-gen-small).
- Average per-token dequant calls reduced by >= 40% for representative streaming workloads.
- Quality regression <= 0.5% measured on the nightly eval prompt set (perplexity and ROUGE for targeted tasks).
- Feature gated and covered by unit + integration tests; deployed behind rollout flag.

Deliverables:
- Kernel catalog schema and initial entries for two common architectures (causal decoder and encoder-decoder attention).
- Runtime scoring module + API for kernel selection.
- Prefill orchestrator that can be toggled per-model.
- Benchmark results, design doc, and a canary rollout plan.
comments: 2026-02-12: Ticket created by Priya after perf spike on INT8 production for low-latency chat workloads. Initial scope and success metrics added.
2026-02-18: Spike results uploaded: microbench harness shows fused-epilogue kernels reduce token wall-time by 18% for seq=64 single-GPU prefill. Link: https://go.redwood/drive/perf/spikes/eng-207321

2026-03-02: Marco implemented initial catalog schema (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/6223). Unit tests for schema validation added. CI perf jobs queued.

2026-03-05: Microbench CI revealed regression on long context (seq=2048) when fused kernels used naive block sizes. Decided to add sequence-length-aware block tuning and a fallback to tiling-based fused kernels.

2026-03-12: Implemented telemetry counters for kernel-switch events and added a scoring weight for KV-cache-warmth. Preparing runtime-1.19 canary manifest. Remaining: perf tuning for long contexts, finalize rollout doc.
implementation_plan:
1) Schema + seed entries (week 1). 2) Scoring service + offline cost matrix ingestion (week 2). 3) Prefill orchestrator + fused-kernel hints (week 3). 4) Canary + iterate (week 4). 5) Rollout and postmortem.

Tasks: create kernel registry table, add microbench harness for sequence/batch/device combos, implement scoring API (/kernel/score), extend scheduler to accept kernel hints, add rollout flag and telemetry dashboards.
tradeoffs_and_risks:
- Fused kernels save copies but increase workspace usage; risk of OOM on memory-constrained nodes. Mitigation: cap workspace and fall back to staged kernels.
- Aggressive kernel switching can cause jitter; mitigate with hysteresis and token-based guard windows.
- Microbench numbers may not reflect real-world composite workloads; will use canary pools and traffic replay for validation.
acceptance_criteria: (1) Performance: P90 <= baseline*0.92 on INT8 popover for target workloads. (2) Correctness: nightly eval <= +0.5% regression. (3) Observability: kernel-switch telemetry, dequant counters, and per-route cost breakdown available in console. (4) Safety: runtime flag and automatic rollback if P99 degrades >10% during canary.
notes: This ticket aims to make kernel selection first-class: treat kernels as tunable primitives with metadata and score-based selection instead of ad-hoc heuristics. It should unlock future features: model-level precision policies, hybrid-precision blends, and autoscaling knobs that account for quantization cost characteristics.
